critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 529 lines and imports many concerns (auth, chat, projects, settings, contact, chat stats). Consider splitting into routers/*.py modules — /app/backend/zoho_portal.py is a good template.

GET /api/chat/stats iterates the full window in Python and does another count_documents on the whole collection each request. For higher volume, replace with a MongoDB aggregation pipeline ($match + $group by date) and cache the total_messages_ever counter, otherwise this endpoint will slow down as chat_messages grows.

chat_stats parses created_at from string with datetime.fromisoformat on every doc — chat_messages should store created_at as native BSON Date (or add a date index) so the range query can use an index; also allows aggregation to work on real dates.

zoho_portal.py: state token is generated but must be validated against the session on /callback — verify the CSRF check exists there (out of scope for this run; not testable without a real OAuth flow).

ZOHO_BOOKS_ORG_ID / ZOHO_PROJECTS_PORTAL_ID / ZOHO_DESK_ORG_ID are empty in .env — portal endpoints will 400 even after a successful OAuth login until these are populated. Consider surfacing this in /api/auth/portal/me as a config_ready flag so the UI can show a clearer error than a generic 400.

Chatbot system prompt still contains legacy Boekweitkamp/Eenmanszaak text (flagged in iteration 4, unresolved). With the new 'Nederland, Delfzijl' branding change this remains inconsistent — chatbot will still spell out the old address.

usePageSeo.js writes to document.head on every route mount — verify it removes/updates existing tags rather than appending duplicates when navigating between pages (a quick spot-check on multiple navigations would confirm no <meta> pileup).
public/sitemap.xml is static — will not include future dynamic project pages. Fine for now, but note if project detail routes are added.
Iteration 4 findings still valid: CORS allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*'; in-memory chat rate store is per-worker.
